info.name: IPRS Backend - Conversation Relay Flow
info.description:
Only the APIs the frontend actually calls for the onboarding flow: OTP auth, then the backend-driven Typebot conversation relay. The frontend never talks to Typebot directly - it only calls /conversation/message and /conversation/upload, and this backend drives Typebot's own Chat API behind the scenes.

## Global envelopes

Success: `{ "success": true, "data": { ... }, "meta"?: { ... } }`

Error: `{ "success": false, "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "details"?: { ... } } }`

Common error codes: `VALIDATION_ERROR` (422, bad request body/params), `UNAUTHORIZED` (401, missing/invalid/expired token), `FORBIDDEN` (403), `NOT_FOUND` (404), `TYPEBOT_NOT_CONFIGURED` (503), `TYPEBOT_REQUEST_FAILED`, `UPLOAD_ERROR` (400, file too large/bad multipart), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (500).

## Flow

1. `POST /auth/send-otp` with a phone number.
2. `POST /auth/verify-otp` with the same phone + the OTP -> get back a JWT `token`. This request's test script auto-saves it into the `{{token}}` collection variable, so every request below is pre-wired.
3. `POST /conversation/message` with an empty body `{}` to start the Typebot session - returns the bot's greeting plus `data.input` describing what to render next.
4. Loop: look at `data.input.type` to decide what UI to show, then respond:
   - `"text input"` / `"email input"` / `"url input"` -> send the user's typed answer as `POST /conversation/message` with `{ "message": "<answer>" }`.
   - `"choice input"` -> send the EXACT text of the chosen `data.input.items[].content` as `{ "message": "<that text>" }`.
   - `"file input"` -> switch to `POST /conversation/upload` (multipart, field name `file`) instead of /message. The backend uploads the file to Typebot's storage, runs OCR when applicable, and advances the conversation for you.
5. Keep looping until the response has no `data.input` (or `data.sessionEnded: true`) - conversation is over.
6. `POST /auth/logout` when the user signs out.

`data.messages` is Typebot's own rich-text message array - render each block's `content.richText` as-is. `data.input` mirrors Typebot's own input-block shape (`id`, `type`, `items` for choices, `options.variableId` when relevant) - pass it through mostly unchanged, don't invent your own shape on top of it.

request.description: phone must match /^\+?[1-9]\d{9,14}$/ (9-14 digits, optional leading +). Rate-limited (stricter auth limiter). In dev (OTP_PROVIDER=mock), data.otp echoes the OTP so you don't need real SMS - omitted when a real SMS provider is configured.

otp must match /^\d{4,6}$/. On success, this request's Test script auto-saves the JWT into {{token}} so every request below Just Works. registrationStatus is 'started' or 'completed' (derived from ApplicationStatus === 1).
Blacklists the current token's jti until its natural expiry. Requires Authorization: Bearer <token>.

Call with an empty body `{}` (or omit `message`) for the very first call to start a session. After that, send `{ "message": "<user's answer>" }` each turn - for choice inputs, `message` must exactly match the chosen item's `content` text. `engine` in the response is 'REGISTRATION' (Typebot relay) or 'AI' (Week-1 stub, only once fully registered). Loop on `data.input` to know what to render next; when `data.input.type === "file input"`, use the Upload request instead of this one.

response.name: 200 OK - first call (session start)
200 OK - continue (choice answer -> next text question)
200 OK - file input step (switch to Upload request)
200 OK - conversation ended (no more input)
503 Service Unavailable (Typebot not configured)

request.description: multipart/form-data, single field named `file`. Only valid when the current conversation step's `data.input.type === "file input"` (from the last /conversation/message response) - otherwise 400 "No active file-upload step in the conversation". Max size = MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB (server config). Response shape is identical to /conversation/message's REGISTRATION-engine result - keep looping the same way afterwards. Do NOT set a Content-Type header manually; let Postman/the HTTP client set the multipart boundary.

response.name: 200 OK - advances to next step
400 Bad Request (no active file-upload step)
